info.name: ADD OS — Identity & Content
info.description:
واجهة برمجية (API) لتطبيق ADD OS - تطبيق إدارة المستخدمين والمحتوى

الميزات الرئيسية:
• مصادقة الأعضاء: رقم الهاتف + كلمة المرور
• مصادقة الموظفين: البريد الإلكتروني + كلمة المرور + مصادقة ثنائية
• نظام الخدمات الديناميكي: ADD Core / Experience / Ecosystem

قبل البدء:
1. استورد بيئة العمل المحلية: ADD OS - Local
2. شغل الخادم: php artisan serve --port=8000

نظام الفرع الافتراضي:
يتم تحديد branch_id تلقائياً من الباك اند (ResolveDefaultBranch).
يمكن تحديد فرع محدد عبر هيدر X-Branch-Id أو branch_id صراحةً.

One request per endpoint. Where an endpoint has several cases (errors, alternative inputs), they are saved examples of that one request, listed under "Cases" in its description.

item.name: Member (App)
item.description: The member mobile app, grouped by feature and numbered in the order a new member meets them. One request per endpoint: other cases (errors, alternative inputs) are saved examples of that request, and are listed under "Cases" in its description.

item.name: 1. Auth
item.description: Sign-up (phone + code), login, token refresh, password recovery, account reactivation and logout. Every other member request needs {{member_token}} from Login or Register — Verify.

request.description:
Step 1 of sign-up. Validates the ENTIRE profile first and only then sends the code أ¢â‚¬â€‌ so "this number already has an account", "that email is taken" and "password too short" all come back as 422 here, before you spend a WhatsApp message and an OTP round trip on a sign-up that was never going to succeed.

On success the profile is parked in `pending_registrations` (password already hashed) so step 2 needs only the phone and the code. Nothing lands in `users` أ¢â‚¬â€‌ an unverified sign-up is never an account. The parked row expires with its code after 5 minutes and is swept hourly by `model:prune`, so abandoning the flow leaves nothing behind and holds no phone number.

Running this again overwrites the parked profile, which is how you correct a typo: fix the field, re-send, use the new code.

There is no `purpose` field أ¢â‚¬â€‌ this endpoint always mints a `registration` code, and Forgot Password always mints a `password_reset` one. A code issued by one is refused by the other with an explicit 422; they are not interchangeable.

Rate-limited (1 per cooldown window per phone per purpose, plus a 10/min per-IP throttle). Code is dispatched via the mock WhatsApp driver أ¢â‚¬â€‌ check storage/logs/laravel.log for the value until a real gateway is wired up.

Step 2 of sign-up, and ACCOUNT CREATION ONLY أ¢â‚¬â€‌ this is no longer the repeat login the old otp/verify was. Returning members use Login.

Just the phone and the code. The profile was validated and parked at step 1, so nothing is re-typed and the password crosses the wire only once. Creates the account, assigns the 'member' role, provisions an empty wallet, and discards the parked row أ¢â‚¬â€‌ all in one transaction.

Returns an access_token + refresh_token pair, both captured automatically. The access token carries the ability `member-app` and nothing more, so it cannot reach /api/v1/admin/* even if the same person is also an operator.

422 "please start signing up again" means there is no parked profile أ¢â‚¬â€‌ step 1 was never run, or it expired along with its code (both last 5 minutes). Re-run step 1.

409 means the number or email was free at step 1 and got claimed in between أ¢â‚¬â€‌ a race, not the normal "already registered" answer, which step 1 gives you as a 422.

Resends the registration OTP to a phone that already has a pending registration (created by **Register â€” Step 1** / Send Code).

Silent on unknown phones (returns 200 with no indication whether the phone has a pending registration).

- **200** â€” Code (re-)sent, or phone has no pending registration (silent).
- **429** â€” Throttled; `retry_after` (seconds) says when to try again.

Use this when the member never received the initial code or it expired.

The everyday sign-in, for MEMBERS ONLY. Returns the same access_token + refresh_token pair sign-up does, both captured automatically. The token carries the ability `member-app`, which /api/v1/admin/* rejects.

401 is deliberately identical for three different failures أ¢â‚¬â€‌ wrong password, unregistered number, and an account that holds no `member` role (an operations or admin account). Operators sign in at Admin/Auth/Login, behind Fortify's second factor; if this endpoint issued them a token, phone + password alone would reach the operations API and the second factor would be worth nothing. The wording is shared so the response can't be used to work out which numbers have accounts, or which of those belong to staff.

403 means the account is deactivated or blocked; no token is issued and the body names the state.

429 after 5 attempts per minute for this phone+IP combination, with retry_after in the body.

Renews an expired access token without the password. Unauthenticated أ¢â‚¬â€‌ the refresh token in the body IS the credential.

Single use: the token sent here is revoked and the previous access token deleted, so both variables are overwritten with the replacements. Sending the same refresh token twice returns 401.

Also 401 if the refresh token has expired (30 days) or the account was deactivated/blocked in the meantime.

Initiates the password reset flow for a registered member.

- **200** â€” Phone belongs to an active member account; a 6-digit reset code has been sent.
- **422** â€” Phone is not registered with any member account.
- **429** â€” OTP request throttled; `retry_after` (seconds) tells you when to try again.

On 200, proceed to **Verify Password Reset** with the code the member receives.

Verifies the 6-digit code sent by **Forgot Password** and authorizes a password reset server-side.

On success the server records a short-lived authorization on the OTP record â€” no token is returned to the client. Proceed directly to **Reset Password** using the same phone number.

Completes the password reset flow.

The server verifies that the OTP for this phone was verified and authorized within the reset window (controlled by `otp.reset_token_ttl_minutes`). No client-side token is required â€” authorization is held server-side.

After a successful reset all existing tokens for the account are revoked; the member must log in again.

Sends an `account_reactivation` code -- only useful to a phone that belongs to a DEACTIVATED member account (that's Member (App)/Account/Deactivate Account, the self-service action that puts it in this state). Always answers 200 with the same neutral message whether or not that applies, same as Forgot Password -- a 200 here is not confirmation anything was sent.

A blocked account never gets a code here -- reversing a block is admin-only (Admin (Dashboard)/Users/Update User Status). Read the code from storage/logs/laravel.log (mock WhatsApp driver) and paste it into Account Reactivation -- Verify.

Restores the account to `active` and signs it straight back in -- unlike Reset Password, this issues a fresh access_token + refresh_token pair (captured automatically), because a deactivated account has no live session to fall back on; there is no separate Login step afterwards.

The code must have been issued by Account Reactivation -- Request Code. A registration or password-reset code sent here is refused with 422 and a message saying so.
Returns profile, roles, permissions, and active status for the currently authenticated member.
Revokes the current access token. Calling Account/Get Me again afterwards should return 401.

item.name: 2. Profile & Account
item.description: The member's own profile, app preferences, privacy consents and account lifecycle.

item.name: Profile
item.description: Read and edit the profile; the completion score and threshold come with it.

request.description: Returns the authenticated member wrapped inside `data.user`: account fields (id, name, phone, email, preferred_language, preferred_currency, status) plus `personal` (`bio`, `city`, `avatar_url`, `gender`), `professional` (`job_title`, `company_name`, `industry`), and `links` (`linkedin_url`, `instagram_url`, `behance_url`, `website_url`). Profile fields are null until the member has ever saved one. Also returns `completion` inside `data`: `score` (0-100) and `threshold` (from the `profile.completion_threshold` setting).

Upserts the personal AND professional profile in one call, in one transaction أ¢â‚¬â€‌ creates both rows on first call, updates them after, never a duplicate row on either table. Every field is optional and independently nullable: omitting a field leaves it unchanged, sending it as `null` explicitly clears it. Send every field together (as in this example) or just the subset you're changing أ¢â‚¬â€‌ both work. Plain single-language strings, not the `{ar, en}` bilingual JSON pattern used for admin-curated content. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success أ¢â‚¬â€‌ not the profile data, since you already sent it; use Get Profile to read it back.

response.name: Avatar Updated

item.name: Preferences
item.description: Language and display currency.

request.description: Updates the authenticated member's stored language preference (`ar`/`en`). Distinct from the `lang` header: the header overrides the response language for this one request; this changes what a future request with no header falls back to. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated user resource.

Updates the authenticated member's stored currency preference (`USD`/`SYP`, display-only أ¢â‚¬â€‌ never affects real pricing/wallet records). Distinct from the `currency` header: the header overrides a plan-listing response's converted currency for this one request; this changes the stored default a request with no header falls back to. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated user resource.

item.name: Privacy & Consent
item.description: The privacy policy and its consent, and the opt-in to the public member directory.

request.description: Records that the signed-in member agreed to the current privacy policy. Reading the policy needs no login: GET /api/v1/privacy-policy.

Returns whether the authenticated member currently has an active `public_directory` consent grant: `{"granted": true|false}`. A member who never granted, or who revoked and never re-granted, gets `false`.

Grants (`granted: true`) or revokes (`granted: false`) the member's consent to appear in the public member directory (see Public (Site) أ¢â€ â€™ Get Member Directory). Consent is append-only history: granting while already active is a no-op, revoking sets `revoked_at` on the active row, and re-granting after a revoke inserts a fresh row rather than reusing the old one. Appearing in the directory also requires at least one filled profile (Personal and/or Professional) and an `active` account status. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success أ¢â‚¬â€‌ use Get Consent Status to read the resulting state back.

item.name: Account
item.description: Password change, deactivation and deletion.

request.description:
The authenticated alternative to Auth/Forgot Password -> Auth/Reset Password: proves identity with `current_password` instead of a WhatsApp code, for a member who already knows it and is signed in. Same password rule as sign-up: min 8 chars, `confirmed`.

422 with `current_password_incorrect` if that field doesn't match -- the password is left unchanged.

On success, every OTHER session this member holds is revoked, but the one making THIS request stays alive -- unlike Reset Password, which ends all of them and issues nothing back. No new token is issued here either, since the current one is still valid; {{member_token}} keeps working as-is.

The example re-uses {{member_password}} for current and new so the variable stays valid for later requests in this collection -- swap in a real new value to test an actual change.

Voluntary, self-service pause -- the member's own counterpart to an admin deactivating/blocking a user (Admin (Dashboard)/Users/Update User Status). `reason` is optional free text, kept for the record. Every session this member holds is revoked, on every device.

Reversible only through Auth/Account Reactivation (a WhatsApp code) -- there is no way back in through Login while `deactivated`. An admin can also reverse it directly, same as a block. Returns `{"message": "..."}`, not the updated user resource.

item.name: 3. Spaces & Bookings
item.description: Browse spaces, read a space's booking setup, pick a date and a run of slots, then preview and book. Order of calls: Browse Spaces → Get Space Details → Day Slots (on each date tapped) → Preview Booking → Create Booking. There is no month calendar endpoint: the app builds the date picker from the setup — open_weekdays from Browse Spaces, upcoming_closures and max_days_ahead from Get Space Details.

item.name: Spaces
item.description: The list carries the branch's hours once (data.working_hours_banner); the details carry this space's booking setup (data.booking).

query.description: Optional: all, co_space (hot_desk), room (meeting_room), business (private_office), event_hall
Optional: Filter spaces by minimum capacity
Optional: Number of spaces per page (default: 10)

request.description:
Returns the active spaces matching the Aleppo Digital District mobile app Browse Spaces UI.

Includes:
- Branch working hours banner — the branch's hours, the same for every space, so stated here once and not in each space's details: today's (text, hours, open_time, close_time, is_open, periods); the ordinary week as `schedule` (days grouped by the hours they share, each group with its own periods and hours, Saturday first), open_weekdays and a translated days_label; and the timezone with its label and note. The upcoming closures are NOT here — they set up the booking calendar, so they come with Get Space Details → data.booking.upcoming_closures. hours/periods are TODAY's only — show the week from `schedule`.
- Badges (OPEN SPACE, MEETING ROOM, PRIVATE OFFICE, EVENT HALL)
- Hourly pricing with currency
- Amenities list with icons
- Pagination: a top-level `meta`, beside `data` — the response is {data: {working_hours_banner, spaces}, meta}

Price (changed 2026-10-02): `price` is the hourly rate in the member's currency with its symbol (`currency` header, else their preference, else the base currency), e.g. "3.00 $ / hour"; `price_point` is the same rate in points, e.g. "30 pts / hour". Both are display-ready; the old `pricing` object (starting_from, hourly_rate, currency, currency_symbol, formatted) is gone.

### Sale
`sale` — null, or while a sale on the hourly rate runs `{points, original_points, original_label, sale_label, discount_points, discount_amount_label, discount_percent, discount_label, ends_at, ends_label}` — `discount_label` is the badge ("20% off"; the amount when under 1%), the percentage rounded down: show the original rate struck through. Price a booking with `bookings/preview`, never rate × duration.

Returns full details for a space matching the mobile app Space Details / Pre-Booking screen.

Includes:
- Badge, title, subtitle, and localized description
- Quick features (Seats, Wi-Fi, Power, Area type)
- Details card (Price per hour, capacity, formatted location hierarchy, branch working hours)
- Amenities checklist (Wi-Fi, Power, Chairs, Printing, Locker, Cafe, plus room equipment)
- Call-to-action button info (Book This Space)
- `booking`: this space's own setup for the booking screen, sent once here — `upcoming_closures` (every date from today on that the branch is closed all day, as ISO-8601 date-times at local midnight with NO offset, e.g. "2026-09-30T00:00:00", to pass straight to DateTime.parse: without an offset it parses as local time, so the 30th stays the 30th on any device — with +03:00 a device in another timezone would move it to the 29th), and `rules` (granularity; min_duration_minutes = the shortest booking LENGTH, with no maximum; min_notice_minutes = the minimum NOTICE before a booking's start, 0 = none — slots inside it are not sent; max_days_ahead = how many days ahead a booking may be made, null = no limit — grey out later dates. The member picks a run of consecutive slots at least min_duration_minutes long; there is no list of lengths). No legend — the app draws its own. The slots endpoint then carries only what changes per date; call it again on each date change. The indicative price of a run of slots is details.price.hourly_rate_points × hours. The branch's week (today's hours and `schedule`) is NOT here — they are the same for every space and come once with the spaces list, in `working_hours_banner`.

item.name: Availability
item.description: Which of the space's slots are free on the date the member tapped. The date picker itself is built on the app from the space's setup — there is no month endpoint.

item.name: Day Slots — Times Free on a Date

query.description: Optional. Enable for the duration-first shape — see the next request.

request.description: The time-slot grid for one date. Response shape: ONE `data` object carrying only what changes per date — {data: {date, state, closed_banner, slots, counts, meta}} — chips under `data.slots`, and `data.date` is just the requested date (Y-m-d), echoed so a stale response can be dropped when dates are tapped quickly. Each slot carries only {start_time, end_time, state, is_available} — the times in 12-hour hh:mm AM|PM (e.g. 03:00 PM, AM/PM in Latin letters in every language), shown as-is and posted back as-is (start_at = "{date} 03:00 PM" is accepted); there is no label in another format — no reason: grey a chip by its state, which for a member is available | booked (taken, every seat taken, inside a buffer, outside hours or beyond the horizon). A slot whose time to be booked has gone — already started, or inside the minimum notice (rules.min_notice_minutes, an hour by default) — is not sent at all: today at 14:00 the list starts at 15:00. Only available is bookable, is_available is exactly state == available, and counts is {available, booked, total}. Each slot is one of the space's own cells (data.meta.granularity_minutes long); there is no duration parameter. To book, the member picks a start slot and an end slot: the run must be unbroken (every slot available, each start_time equal to the previous end_time) and at least rules.min_duration_minutes long — there is no maximum; post start_at = "{date} {first.start_time}", end_at = "{date} {last.end_time}". data.meta is {granularity_minutes, timezone}. The indicative price is the details' hourly_rate_points × hours — the amount actually charged, after discount and VAT, is what bookings/preview returns. The calendar setup is NOT here: the branch's week comes once from the spaces list's working_hours_banner, and this space's rules and upcoming_closures (local-midnight date-times) from Get Space Details → data.booking; then call this again on each date change. The desk's route returns this very body, byte for byte. Each chip is judged on its own — is this stretch free — so the cell right before another booking is available: it can end a run even though no minimum-length booking could start there. Slots are generated only inside the day's open periods, so a two-period day has no chips across the midday gap.

item.name: Bookings
item.description: Preview, create (one date or several), list, read, extend and cancel. Each error case is a saved example of its request.

request.description:
Builds the confirmation screen WITHOUT creating anything: price breakdown (N hours × rate, subtotal, VAT from booking.vat_percent, total), the payment methods, and the note field. Every spendable wallet is listed — one that cannot cover the cost comes back with sufficient:false rather than being omitted — plus a synthetic `cash` option, which is what PaymentState::Unpaid plus reception settlement already means. `unavailable_reason` is the exact message POST bookings would return for the same window.

### Coupon (optional)
`coupon_code` — leave it empty for none. A code that cannot be used refuses the request with 422 `{message, reason}` (`reason` = not_found | not_started | expired | usage_limit_reached | per_user_limit_reached | not_eligible | new_members_only | not_applicable | min_amount_not_met | not_combinable | already_applied | payment_in_progress). The response carries `coupon: {code, applied, points_discounted, message}`; `applied: false` with a message means the current offer was already lower. The breakdown gains `sale` and `coupon` lines. **The app should show this total rather than computing rate × duration itself** — a sale can cover part of a booking.

docs/decisions/booking-creation-approval-extension.md. Creates a confirmed+unpaid booking when the space has no wallet balance and requires_approval = false (made with a card it is created `awaiting_payment` instead — see Held for its prepayment below). 201 returns the created booking and auto-captures booking_id.

### Cases — see this request's saved examples
- **Error: Invalid Start Time** — 422 `{"message": "The start time does not match this space's slot granularity."}`
- **Error: Slot Unavailable** — 422 `{"message": "This space is not available for the requested time."}` when a confirmed or pending booking already covers this window.
- **Error: Multiple Wallets, Choice Required** — 422 `{"message": "More than one wallet can cover this booking. Please choose one.", "wallet_options": [...]}` when both a personal and a company balance apply -- resubmit with wallet_owner_type/wallet_owner_id from the list (see Wallet > Get Wallet Options).
- **Error: Start in the Past** — 422 api.booking.start_in_the_past. Closes a trap where a past-dated booking could be created and paid for and then never cancelled, its cancellation window having long gone. A booking starting this very minute is still fine. Overridable via the booking.allow_past_bookings setting.
- **Error: Outside the Booking Window** — The booking window, two rules (a booking's length has no maximum):
• booking.max_days_ahead → 422 api.booking.too_far_ahead (start date beyond today + N local days). 0 = no limit, the default.
• booking.min_notice_minutes → 422 api.booking.too_soon (start closer to now than N minutes). Seeded at 60; 0 turns it off.
Checked right after the past-start rule, before business hours. They apply to reception bookings too (same BookingCreationService), to bookings/batch (per-window reason too_far_ahead / too_soon) and to bookings/preview (as unavailable_reason). The calendar projects the same rules as slot states too_soon / too_far_ahead and day state out_of_range.

Also 422 api.booking.space_not_bookable when the space is under maintenance or retired (e.g. taken out of service after the booking screen opened) — on create, on bookings/batch (per-window reason space_not_bookable) and on bookings/preview (as unavailable_reason). The read endpoints 404 such a space.

### Paying (unified payments)
`payment_method` (required): wallet (pay now, or 422 with current/required/shortage and no booking), cash (unpaid, settled at reception), paymera (a hold — `status: awaiting_payment` with a `payment_due_at` deadline — then its card payment opens: `payment` and `redirect_url` beside `data`).

If the card cannot be started, the hold still stands until `payment_due_at`, with `payment: null` and `payment_error` — the member can pay again with the booking's id (below), or choose cash or the wallet. `bookings/batch` takes wallet or cash only.

**`payment_method` is required** — the method the member picked from Get Payment Methods (`wallet` | `cash` | `paymera`; batch: `wallet` | `cash`). Omitting it → 422 and nothing is booked.

### Coupon (optional)
`coupon_code` — leave it empty for none. A code that cannot be used refuses the request with 422 `{message, reason}` (`reason` = not_found | not_started | expired | usage_limit_reached | per_user_limit_reached | not_eligible | new_members_only | not_applicable | min_amount_not_met | not_combinable | already_applied | payment_in_progress). The response carries `coupon: {code, applied, points_discounted, message}`; `applied: false` with a message means the current offer was already lower. The coupon is used once the booking holds its slot; cancelling gives it back.

### Paying again — send the request again with the booking's id
`booking_id` is `null` (or left out) when creating — a new booking is made. A booking is made first, then paid. To pay it another way — after a failed card, or later (a cash booking paid in the app) — send this same request again with `booking_id` (the `data.id` of the first response) and the new `payment_method` (plus `wallet_owner_type`/`wallet_owner_id`, `coupon_code` if needed). Nothing is created and no creation rule runs (start in the past, booking window, hours, granularity, availability): only how it is paid changes, so a request sent minutes before the start is never refused as too soon. `space_id`, `start_at` and `end_at` are optional then; any that are sent must equal the booking's, else 422 `booking_mismatch`.

Answers 200 `{data: <the booking>, payment, redirect_url, next, coupon?}` — `next` is `redirect` | `done` | `pay_at_reception`. Errors: 404 not the member's booking · 409 already paid · 422 `booking_not_payable` (cancelled, rejected, no-show — or an `awaiting_payment` whose `payment_due_at` passed) · 422 `{message, current, required, shortage}` when the wallet is short · 502/503 card payment unavailable (not a declined card).

### Held for its prepayment — `awaiting_payment`
A booking made with a prepaid method (`paymera` today; any gateway key in `config/payments.php`) is a **hold**: `status: awaiting_payment` and `payment_due_at = min(now + 15 minutes, start_at)` (`PAYMENTS_PREPAYMENT_WINDOW_MINUTES`). It holds the slot but is not confirmed — door codes, QR unlock and the reception lists and counts ignore it; reception cannot check it in (409 `api.booking.check_in_awaiting_payment`: take the payment first) and a coworking scan tells the member to pay it first. The confirm screen shows a countdown from `payment_due_at`, which the member booking list and detail carry too.

It is released — `payment_due_at` cleared — when the card is accepted, when it is paid from the wallet, or when the member switches to cash by sending this request again with `booking_id`: the booking becomes `confirmed` (`pending` if the space needs approval; the operations "pending approval" notice is sent then, not at creation). Sending it again with another prepaid method opens a new card **without** extending the deadline.

The member may cancel a hold at any time (Cancel Booking), even inside the cancellation window. Creating a booking for another time on the same space (no `booking_id`) cancels the member's own overlapping hold; a real `confirmed` or `pending` booking still blocks.

Past `payment_due_at`, `payments:cancel-expired-prepayments` (every minute, after one last gateway check) cancels the hold: `status: cancelled`, `status_note` "payment not completed" (`api.booking.status_notes.payment_not_completed`), and the member is notified. Sending the request again with its `booking_id` then answers 422 `booking_not_payable` and the member starts again. A card already in flight that the bank accepts before the cancellation still pays it; one accepted after becomes points in the wallet with the payment `needs_review`.

request.description:
**Multi-date** (the request as saved). The multi-select date strip: up to 10 windows, ALL OR NOTHING. Partial success would leave the member part-charged for a booking they never got, so any failure rolls the whole batch back and nothing is debited. Windows already accepted earlier in the same batch are checked against each other too. The wallet is debited ONCE for the summed total.

### Cases — see this request's saved examples
- **Batch Error: One Date Taken** — 422 with a per-window `errors` array naming each bad window by its index in the submitted list, so the app can mark the offending chip. These two windows overlap EACH OTHER — neither is in the database yet, so a check against stored rows alone would pass both. Nothing is created.

**`payment_method` is required** — the method the member picked from Get Payment Methods (`wallet` | `cash` | `paymera`; batch: `wallet` | `cash`). Omitting it → 422 and nothing is booked.

### Coupon (optional)
`coupon_code` — leave it empty for none. A code that cannot be used refuses the request with 422 `{message, reason}` (`reason` = not_found | not_started | expired | usage_limit_reached | per_user_limit_reached | not_eligible | new_members_only | not_applicable | min_amount_not_met | not_combinable | already_applied | payment_in_progress). The response carries `coupon: {code, applied, points_discounted, message}`; `applied: false` with a message means the current offer was already lower. One use per window, while the code's limits allow (a limit of 2 over 3 windows refuses the request).

request.description:
The member's own bookings, filtered on their `status`, as `{data, meta}` — no per-tab counts.

`status`: one key, or several comma-separated (`status=pending,confirmed` is the design's "Upcoming" tab in one request); omitted, every booking; an unknown key is a 422. There is no `filter` key any more — one sent is ignored. `meta.total` is the total for the statuses asked for and `meta.status` echoes them (`[]` for all).

Each card carries only what the card draws: `id`, `space {title, main_image}` (`title` falls back to the space browser's per-type title when the space has no name), `date_label` ("Today, …" / "Tomorrow, …" / the date, in the request's `lang`), `time_label` ("01:00 PM - 02:00 PM (1h)"), `is_upcoming` (true until the booking starts), `status`, `status_label`, `payment_state` (`paid | unpaid`). `cancellation` is null when the booking cannot be cancelled; otherwise `deadline_label`, and `refund_points` / `refund_price` / `refund_to` — exactly what cancelling gives back and to which wallet ("Your wallet" or the company). 403 for another member's booking. See docs/decisions/booking-outcomes-and-extension.md.

`discounts`: what was taken off it, as locked when it was priced; renaming or changing the offer later does not rewrite it. One entry per kind: `offer` (`offer_id`), `coupon` (`coupon_id`, `code`), `plan_discount` (`plan_discount_id`), `duration_saving` (a plan's built-in saving; takes nothing off, `name` = what it was compared to). How far the member's running booking can be extended, and at what price. Extendable only while it runs (start_at ≤ now < end_at), checked in and not out, on a space with `allows_extension`. `latest_end_at` is the latest the member can stay: the next booking less its buffer, a co-working loan, the seat pool, or the branch's closing — whichever comes first. Gap found in the Task 15 Postman audit. Debits the buyer's personal wallet (or, with an optional company_id, the company's wallet -- requires CompanyPolicy::manageMembers) for plan.price and creates the Membership in one transaction. `payment_method`: wallet (default) or paymera — **no cash: there is no subscription without payment** (422 on `cash`; a member who wants to pay cash tops up at reception and buys with points).

The membership is created **only when the card is accepted**; a failed or cancelled card subscribes nothing, and the member starts again.

This is the one request that buys a plan; there is no generic payments endpoint.

### Coupon (optional)
`coupon_code` — leave it empty for none. A code that cannot be used refuses the request with 422 `{message, reason}` (`reason` = not_found | not_started | expired | usage_limit_reached | per_user_limit_reached | not_eligible | new_members_only | not_applicable | min_amount_not_met | not_combinable | already_applied | payment_in_progress). request.description:
One row as a receipt: everything the list row has, plus:

- `reference` — e.g. `TRX-20261003-000214`, for the member to quote to support.
- `balance.before` / `balance.after` — the balance of the row's own pool (`category_label`, e.g. General balance) just before and just after it, as points with money labels.
- `paid` — for money that came in (a card or cash top-up, or a payment taken at reception): what was actually charged or handed over, verbatim `{amount, currency, label}`; null otherwise.
- `expires_at` — for categorized points that expire; null for General.
- `paid_at` — when the payment the row belongs to went through (ISO 8601, local time +03:00), or null when no payment is behind the row. Usually the same moment as `created_at`; for a `refund` row it is the original payment's date, while `created_at` is when it was refunded. The payment itself is Get Payment Status.

`points` is a signed string, as in the list: `"+1000"` for a credit, `"-120"` for a spend.

Reaching it from a payment: every payment now carries `transaction_id` (Get Payment Status) — the row it shows up as in the history (the spend, or for a top-up the credit); null until it settles. So the "payment successful" screen can open this receipt directly.

Only rows of the member's own personal wallet: anything else is a 404, not a 403, so ids cannot be probed.

item.description:
Topping up the member's own wallet by card, in the order the app calls it:

1. **Get Top-up Options** — the methods (the card only) and the minimum amount.
2. **Top Up Wallet** — opens the card payment; open `redirect_url` in a WebView.
3. **Get Top-up Status** — poll after the WebView closes until `accepted` (the points are credited).

Paymera tells the server too (**Payment Gateway (called by Paymera)**); the app never calls those. Cash for points is taken at reception (**Admin (Dashboard) › Reception Operations › Wallet Top-up**), not in the app.

Get Payment Methods with `purpose=wallet_top_up` — what the top-up screen offers. A member tops up by a prepaid method only: today the card (`paymera`) alone — never `wallet` (points cannot buy points) and never `cash` (cash for points is taken by reception, not the app).

`min_top_up` `{points, amount, currency}`: the card's floor — 10 points by default (`PAYMENTS_MIN_TOP_UP_POINTS`) — and what it costs in the charged currency, as a whole amount (e.g. `"13840"`). Show it on the card form. Null when the charge currency has no exchange rate yet.

Then pay with **2. Top Up Wallet**.

request.description:
Tops up the member's personal wallet through a payment gateway. `payment_method` is **required**: send the `key` of the method the member picked from **1. Get Top-up Options** as it is — today only `paymera` (the card), so a gateway added later works with no app change. Missing, `cash`, `wallet`, or a gateway that is switched off → 422 on `payment_method`: cash for points is taken by reception (admin `POST reception/wallet-top-ups`), not through the app.

`amount` is in MAJOR units of the charged currency (SYP) — no minor units, separators or currency symbol, a plain decimal (`10` or `10.50`, never `1e3`). Read the floor first from **1. Get Top-up Options** (`min_top_up`); below it → 422 on `amount`: "The minimum top-up is 13,840 SYP (10 points)."

Returns 201 `{data: {payment, redirect_url, next: "redirect"}}`. Open `redirect_url` in a WebView, then poll **Get Payment Status**; once `accepted`, its `transaction_id` is the credit row — open it with Wallet › Get Wallet Transaction.

503 = gateway unavailable (our misconfiguration, e.g. no active USD->SYP exchange rate). 502 = could not start. Neither is a declined card — nothing was charged.

### Cases — see this request's saved examples
- **Top-up by card** — 201, `next: redirect`.
- **Error: Top-up Below the Minimum** — 422 on `amount`.
- **Error: Cash Is Reception's** — 422 on `payment_method`.
- **Error: Method Missing** — 422 on `payment_method`.

request.description:
The top-up's status — the same endpoint as **Payments › Get Payment Status**, here for the top-up flow. Poll it with the `payment.id` that **2. Top Up Wallet** returned (saved to `{{payment_id}}`) once the WebView closes: `accepted` → the points are in the wallet (refresh **Wallet › Get Wallet**); `pending` → poll again; `failed` / `canceled` / `expired` → nothing was credited.

Poll this after the WebView closes. The server re-syncs with the gateway on every read; the call is locked and idempotent, so polling cannot double-credit.

NOTE the shape differs from the create response: the payment is at `data` here, not `data.payment`.

status: pending (keep polling) | accepted (success) | failed | canceled | expired | needs_review (NOT a failure — money taken, needs support) | reversed.

charged_amount is the whole amount charged in `currency`, as sent to the gateway.

A member may only read their own payments; anyone else's is a 404, not a 403, so ids cannot be probed.

Call it when the WebView reaches `/paymera/callback/` (then close the WebView), or when the member closes it. Act on `data.status`: `accepted` success · `pending` poll every 2–3 s for ~30 s · `failed`/`canceled`/`expired` show retry · `needs_review` under review · `reversed` refunded. Never read the WebView page itself.

`discounts`: what was taken off it, as locked when it was priced; renaming or changing the offer later does not rewrite it. One entry per kind: `offer` (`offer_id`), `coupon` (`coupon_id`, `code`), `plan_discount` (`plan_discount_id`), `duration_saving` (a plan's built-in saving; takes nothing off, `name` = what it was compared to). request.description:
تسجيل العضو الحالي في الفعالية. تؤخذ بيانات العضو تلقائياً من حسابه (الاسم، البريد، الهاتف). في الفعاليات المجانية يتم التسجيل الفوري، وفي الفعاليات المدفوعة يتم خصم سعر الفعالية بالنقاط (price_points) مباشرة من محفظة العضو.

### Cases — see this request's saved examples
- **answering the form** — Answers are validated against the event's stored field definitions. Submitting name/phone/email is refused with 422 — they come from the token.
- **profile only** — Most events need nothing the account does not already hold. An empty body is valid; check has_registration_form on the details endpoint first.

### Paying (unified payments)
`payment_method` (optional, default the member's own wallet as before) and `wallet_owner_type`/`wallet_owner_id`. For a paid event: wallet pays now (short = the old `points` validation error); cash confirms the seat (`approved`) **unpaid** — the door refuses check-in until it is paid; paymera holds it as `awaiting_payment` with a `payment_due_at` deadline (below), and the response adds `payment` and `redirect_url` inside `data`. An event that needs approval stores the choice and charges the wallet at approval.

### Coupon (optional)
`coupon_code` — leave it empty for none. A code that cannot be used refuses the request with 422 `{message, reason}` (`reason` = not_found | not_started | expired | usage_limit_reached | per_user_limit_reached | not_eligible | new_members_only | not_applicable | min_amount_not_met | not_combinable | already_applied | payment_in_progress). What the registration costs after the code is the registration's own `price_points`; the event's `price_points` stays its list price. A coupon that makes the event free confirms the seat as paid.

### Paying again — send the request again with the ticket's id
A registration is made first, then paid. To pay it another way — after a failed card, or later (an approved, unpaid seat) — send this request again with `ticket_id` (the `data.ticket_id` of the first response) and `payment_method` (plus `wallet_owner_type`/`wallet_owner_id`, `coupon_code`). **No form is sent**: nothing is registered and the registration window, the full flag, capacity and form rules do not run.

Answers 200 `{data: {ticket_id, status, payment, redirect_url, next, coupon?}}`. A registration still **pending approval** (and unpaid) only has its stored choice updated — `next: pay_at_reception`, `payment: null`, nothing charged until approval. Errors: 404 not the member's registration for this event · 409 already paid · 422 `{message, current, required, shortage}` when the wallet is short · 422 `registration_not_payable` (a rejected registration, or an `awaiting_payment` whose `payment_due_at` passed) · 502/503 card payment unavailable. Without a `ticket_id`, registering again for an event the member already holds a seat in is still `already_registered`.

### Held for its prepayment — `awaiting_payment`
A registration approved on the spot for a paid event (and not made free by a coupon) and paid by a prepaid method (`paymera` today; any gateway key in `config/payments.php`) is a **hold**: `status: awaiting_payment`, with `payment_due_at = min(now + 15 minutes, the event's start)` in the result's `data`. It holds the seat but is not approved, so the door refuses check-in until it is paid. It is released to `approved` (`payment_due_at` cleared) when the card is accepted, when it is paid from the wallet, or when the member switches to cash by sending this request again with `ticket_id`. Past the deadline `payments:cancel-expired-prepayments` rejects it ("Your seat was released because the payment was not completed in time", `api.event.prepayment_expired`) and notifies the member; sending `ticket_id` again then answers 422 `registration_not_payable` and the member registers again. A registration that needs approval is unchanged: `pending`, no card at registration, paid after approval by sending `ticket_id`.

item.name: 11. Coworking Sessions
item.description:
Self-service coworking sessions, co_space only: scan the kiosk's rotating code to start, watch the timer, ask to end, read the report. Rooms and other spaces keep their own flow. See docs/decisions/coworking-self-service-sessions.md.

Flow: Start Session → (422 confirmation_required → Start Session again with scan_ticket + accept_uncovered) → Current Session for the timer → Request End → reception confirms → the member gets a coworking.session_ended notification → Session Report.

To run it end to end from Postman: Admin → Kiosks → Create Kiosk → Issue Pairing Code, then Kiosk (device app) → Pair Kiosk. That saves kiosk_id and kiosk_secret, and Start Session builds the kiosk's current code itself.

exec: // The kiosk's current code, built from kiosk_secret (saved by "Pair Kiosk") the way the kiosk app does it: RFC 6238, HMAC-SHA1, 30 s, 8 digits.
// Leaves coworking_qr_value alone when there is no secret, so a value scanned off a real kiosk can be pasted in instead.

request.description:
**Scan the kiosk's code** (the request as saved). qr_value is what the kiosk's QR holds: `add-cowork:v1:{kiosk_id}:{8-digit code}`; a code is accepted during its 30 s step and one step either side. The pre-request script builds {{coworking_qr_value}} from kiosk_secret (saved by Kiosk (device app) → Pair Kiosk); without a secret, paste a scanned value into that variable.

Checked in this order: the code (or ticket) → the kiosk's space is an active co_space → business hours → you already have an open coworking session (200 with it — scanning twice is harmless) → a confirmed booking of yours on this space today that starts within 15 minutes or has started is checked in (type booking) → otherwise a walk-in: started at once when your plan covers it, else 422 confirmation_required. Coverage reasons: no_plan, plan_expired, plan_without_hours, hours_exhausted, outside_window. Throttled to 10 per minute. Saves coworking_session_type and coworking_session_id on 200/201, and scan_ticket on 422 confirmation_required.

### Cases — see this request's saved examples
- **Plan Covers It** — 201 walk-in; coverage.status covered, coverage.covered_until is when the plan stops covering it (window end or hours running out, whichever first).
- **Confirmation Required** — 422 with reason, coverage, hourly_rate_points and a scan_ticket valid 120 s. Nothing has started. Show the message and ask the member.
- **Accept Uncovered** — body `{"scan_ticket": "…", "accept_uncovered": true}` → 201 paid walk-in, accepted_uncovered true. Coverage is evaluated again at this moment (a renewal in between makes it covered).
- **Already in a Session** — 200 with the open session, nothing new started.
- **Booking Checked In** — 201, type booking — your booking on this space was checked in instead of a walk-in.
- **Error: Booking Awaiting Approval** — 409 `{"message":"Your booking is awaiting approval. Please see reception."}` — no walk-in fallback, which would route around approval.
- **Error: Ticket Expired** — 422 `{"message":"This confirmation has expired. Scan the kiosk code again."}` — also for a ticket that is not yours or was tampered with.
- **Error: Invalid Code** — 422 `{"message":"This code is not valid. Scan the code currently shown on the kiosk."}` — wrong, too old, malformed, or from an inactive/unpaired kiosk.
- **Error: Kiosk Unavailable** — 422 `{"message":"Coworking sessions are not available at this kiosk right now."}` — the kiosk's space is not an active co_space (e.g. under maintenance).
- **Error: Outside Business Hours** — 422 `{"message":"This action is not available outside business hours."}`
- **Error: No Capacity** — 422 `{"message":"This space has no available capacity right now."}`

item.description:
Discount coupons (docs/decisions/pricing-offers-and-coupons.md). Reads are open to admin and operations; create, update and delete are admin-only and audited (`coupon_created` / `coupon_updated` / `coupon_deleted`).

- `code`: letters, digits, `-` and `_`, stored upper-case; members type it in any case.
- `discount_type`: `percentage` (1–100) or `amount_off` (points). `max_discount_points` caps a percentage; `min_amount_points` is compared with the price after any offer.
- `combinable_with_offers: false` — the code is weighed against the list price instead of stacking on a sale/plan discount; when the offer is already lower the purchase goes through at the offer price with `coupon.applied: false`.
- Who: `user_ids` (none = anyone), `company_id` (that company's members), `new_members_only`, `usage_limit` (first N uses), `per_user_limit` (defaults to 1 on create; send null for unlimited).
- What: `targets` (none = every purchase a coupon can be spent on — never a wallet top-up). Each target is a `purpose` (`booking` | `coworking_session` | `plan_purchase` | `event_registration`) and at most one item: `plan_id` for a plan, `space_id` or `space_type` for time in a space, `event_id` for an event.
- `starts_at`/`ends_at` are local (Damascus) wall-clock times, like every other typed time.

Uses are counted live from the record they are on: cancelling a booking, a failed card or an expired cash hold gives the use back.
- `locked: true` (List/Get): the coupon or offer has been used, so it can only be switched on/off (`Set Coupon Active`); editing it is 409 `api.coupon.used_locked` and deleting it 409 `api.coupon.has_redemptions`.

The owner's point balance plus its value in the requested currency, for the top-up dialog and the receipt view. Exactly one of user_id / company_id. Every currency figure is derived from the stored point count, so a receipt can never claim a value the wallet does not hold.

`data.top_up` carries everything the dashboard needs to quote a top-up locally: `point_rate_usd` (always a 4-decimal string, e.g. "0.1000"), `min_points`, and `currencies[]` — one per active currency that has a current rate — with `code`, `rate_to_base` ("1" for the base currency), `cash_step` (smallest amount the till takes, e.g. "1.00") and `decimal_places`.

What selling this plan for cash would take, without writing anything: `list_points`, `points` (the price now, a running offer included) and `payment_amount` — that price in `payment_currency`, by the same conversion the sale collects with. Same body as the sale. Also `balance_points` (the owner's general points) and `wallet_covers` — offer `payment_method: wallet` only when it is true. `offer` names the running offer that priced it (`name`, `discount_type`, `discount_value`, `saved_points`, `ends_at`), null when none; `coupon` is the outcome of `coupon_code` (`applied`, `points_discounted`, `message`), null when none was sent. **Sell a plan at the desk** — for cash, or (`payment_method: wallet`) from the points the owner already holds when they cover the whole price (no mixing). For cash it works, the way a wallet is topped up (docs/decisions/unified-payments.md, "Plans sold for cash at reception"). No `amount`: the desk takes the plan's price exactly, in `currency` (default: the base currency). The money becomes points in the owner's wallet — `user_id` or `company_id`, exactly one — and is spent on the plan at once; the subscription is active on 201.

The 201 is a receipt: `transaction_code` (`PLN-…`), `points_charged`, `payment_amount`/`payment_currency`, balances before and after, `membership`, `payment`.

- 422 `{message, reason}` — the coupon cannot be used.
- 422 + `current`/`required`/`shortage` — `wallet` chosen and the points do not cover the price; nothing is recorded.
- 422 `message` — the owner already has an active membership.
- 422 `plan_id` — inactive, or a one-time package.
- 422 `company_id` — inactive company.
- 422 + `first_shortfall_at` — the branch's co-working pool is full; nothing is recorded.
- 422 — the currency has no exchange rate.

Called by the kiosk app, no login. Trades a pairing code (Admin → Kiosks → Issue Pairing Code; case, spaces and dashes are ignored) for the kiosk's TOTP secret — the only response that ever carries it, sent with Cache-Control: no-store. Every pairing generates a new secret, so pairing a replacement device cuts off the old one. Throttled to 5 per minute. Saves kiosk_id and kiosk_secret (Member → 11. Coworking Sessions → Start Session uses them).

What the kiosk app does with it: keep `secret` in secure storage (Keychain / Keystore), never in plain preferences or logs; show a QR holding `{qr_prefix}:{kiosk_id}:{code}` where code = TOTP(secret) with `totp.algorithm` / `totp.digits` / `totp.period` (SHA1, 8, 30 — any RFC 6238 library), refreshed every period; keep the device clock NTP-synced (one step of drift is tolerated). It never calls the API again after pairing.

- **Error: Invalid or Expired Code** — 422 `{"message":"This pairing code is invalid or has expired."}` — the same answer for a wrong, expired or already-used code and for an inactive kiosk.
